'''Tie''': {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Lawton Chiles]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Jeb Bush]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 49.5%{{cite web |url=https://results.elections.myflorida.com/Index.asp?ElectionDate=11/3/1998&DATAMODE=|title=November 3, 1998 General Election|website=Florida Department of State|access-date=2022-05-15}} }} {{ElectionsFL}} The '''1998 Florida gubernatorial election''' was held on November 3, 1998, to determine the [[Governor of Florida|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Florida|lieutenant governor of Florida]]. Democratic incumbent [[Lawton Chiles]] was term-limited and could not run for re-election. [[Jeb Bush]], who had run for governor in [[1994 Florida gubernatorial election|1994]], defeated [[Lieutenant Governor of Florida|lieutenant governor]] [[Buddy MacKay]] by nearly 11 percent of the vote. Primary elections were held on September 1. The primary campaign was largely uneventful, as MacKay and Bush officially ran unopposed for their respective nominations.{{cite news|url=http://www.cnn.com/ALLPOLITICS/1998/09/02/florida.results/|title=Florida Primary Results -- Sept. 1, 1998|publisher=CNN.com|date=September 1, 1998|access-date=October 15, 2014}} The lack of competitiveness saw a very low turnout of just 16.6% of voters for the primary.{{cite news|url=http://politics.heraldtribune.com/2014/08/29/florida-voter-turnout-worst-16-years/|title=Florida voter turnout was worst in 16 years|publisher=Herald Tribune|first=Lloyd|last=Dunkelberger|date=August 29, 2014|access-date=October 15, 2014}} Bush was one of four Republicans to gain a governorship for their party in the [[1998 United States gubernatorial elections|1998 gubernatorial elections]]. With his win, Republicans won a trifecta in the state for the first time since 1875. This was the second election in which MacKay had unsuccessfully run to succeed Chiles, the first being the [[1988 United States Senate election in Florida|1988 Senate race]]. == Democratic primary == === Candidates === * [[Buddy MacKay]], incumbent [[Lieutenant Governor of Florida|lieutenant governor of Florida]] ==== Withdrew ==== * [[Rick Dantzler]], state senator from [[Winter Haven, Florida|Winter Haven]]{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/politics/campaigns/keyraces98/stories/fl053098.htm|title=In Fla. Race, Jeb Bush Finds 'Kinder, Gentler' Plays Well|newspaper=The Washington Post|first=Terry|last=Neal|date=May 30, 1998|access-date=October 15, 2014}} (''ran for lieutenant governor'') * [[J. Keith Arnold]], state representative from [[Fort Myers, Florida|Fort Myers]]{{cite news|url=https://doe.dos.state.fl.us/elections/resultsarchive/DetailRpt.Asp?ELECTIONDATE=9/1/1998&RACE=EDU&PARTY=DEM&DIST=&GRP=&DATAMODE=|archive-url=https://archive.today/20141015164640/https://doe.dos.state.fl.us/elections/resultsarchive/DetailRpt.Asp?ELECTIONDATE=9/1/1998&RACE=EDU&PARTY=DEM&DIST=&GRP=&DATAMODE=|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 15, 2014|title=September 1, 1998 Primary Election: Democratic Primary|publisher=Florida Department of State: Division of Elections|access-date=October 15, 2014}} (''[[1998 Florida Education Commissioner election|ran for education commissioner]]'') === Campaign === Initially the Democratic primary saw a three-way race between MacKay, [[Rick Dantzler]] and [[J. Keith Arnold]], but the latter two dropped out early. Dantzler became MacKay's running mate, and Arnold ran for [[Florida Department of Education|Education Commissioner]]. === Results === {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Buddy MacKay]] | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 1,244,044 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} == Republican primary == === Candidates === * [[Jeb Bush]], businessman, [[1994 Florida gubernatorial election|1994 nominee]], and member of the [[Bush family]] === Results === {{Election box begin no change | title = Republican primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Jeb Bush]] | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 998,566 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==General election== === Candidates === *[[Jeb Bush]], businessman, 1994 nominee, and member of the [[Bush family]] (Republican) **Running mate: [[Frank Brogan]], [[Florida Department of Education|Florida education commissioner]] *[[Buddy MacKay]], incumbent [[Lieutenant Governor of Florida|lieutenant governor of Florida]] (Democratic) **Running mate: [[Rick Dantzler]], state senator from [[Winter Haven, Florida|Winter Haven]] === Campaign === Jeb Bush enjoyed double-digit leads in polling through most of the campaign, and had a large fundraising advantage over MacKay.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/10/23/us/the-1998-campaign-florida-in-race-for-governor-democrat-is-in-trouble.html|title=THE 1998 CAMPAIGN: FLORIDA; In Race for Governor, Democrat Is in Trouble|work=The New York Times|first=Mireya|last=Navarro|date=October 23, 1998|access-date=October 15, 2014}} Bush attempted to revamp his image after appearing too hard-right during the 1994 race. Internal struggles amongst key Democratic constituencies, particularly the African-American community, hurt MacKay. MacKay and the Florida Democratic party drew the ire of the black community after state representative [[Willie Logan]], poised to become the first black [[Speaker (politics)|speaker]] of the [[Florida House of Representatives|Florida House]], was ousted by party leaders. Logan endorsed Bush in the general election. Meanwhile, after receiving only 5% of the African-American vote in 1994, Bush sought to connect to minorities,{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-nov-01-mn-38344-story.html|title=Jeb Bush Reaching Out in Florida|work=Los Angeles Times|first=Mike|last=Clary|date=November 1, 1998|access-date=October 15, 2014}} a group he admittedly ignored in 1994. Setting a tone of [[compassionate conservatism]], and portraying himself as a "consensus-building pragmatist,"{{cite news|url=https://www.economist.com/united-states/1998/10/15/listening-jeb-bush|title=Listening Jeb Bush|newspaper=The Economist|date=October 15, 1998|access-date=October 15, 2014}} he met with African American leaders, and reached out to Jews and Hispanics. He introduced his Mexican-born wife [[Columba Bush|Columba]] on the campaign trail, and demonstrated his fluent bi-lingual abilities, particularly in [[South Florida]]. MacKay ran from behind for the entire race, and barely managed closed to gap to ten points in the days leading up to the general election. On election day, Bush won by almost 11%. He garnered 61% of the Hispanic vote and 14% of the African American vote, a surprising showing for a Republican seeking statewide office. With his brother [[George W. Bush]] [[1998 Texas gubernatorial election|winning re-election in Texas]], the two brothers became the first siblings to govern two states at the same time since [[Nelson Rockefeller|Nelson]] and [[Winthrop Rockefeller]] governed [[New York (state)|New York]] and [[Arkansas]] from 1967 to 1971. Despite his strong statewide showing, Bush was unable to provide [[Coattail effect|coattails]] for other Republicans further down the ticket. [[Charlie Crist]] was easily defeated in [[1998 United States Senate election in Florida|his Senate race]], and [[1998 United States House of Representatives elections|House]] Republicans did not pick up any seats in the [[Midterm election|midterms]]. In the [[Florida Legislature|state legislature]], the GOP netted no new [[Florida Senate|Senate]] seats, and picked up only two seats in the [[Florida House of Representatives|House]]. A little over a month after the election, [[Lawton Chiles]] died suddenly of a heart attack. [[Buddy MacKay]], still the sitting [[Lieutenant Governor of Florida|lieutenant governor]], was sworn in as the 42nd governor of Florida on December 13, 1998, and served out the final 23 days of Chiles' second term. In an ironic twist, MacKay managed to serve in the office he lost the race for, but stated "There's no great pleasure in this."{{cite news|url=http://www.sptimes.com/State/121498/MacKay_steps_into_awk.html|title=MacKay steps into awkward 23 days|publisher=St. Petersburg Times|first=Peter|last=Wallsten|date=December 14, 1998|access-date=October 15, 2014}} MacKay oversaw the state funeral of Chiles, and made a handful of minor appointments, before Bush was sworn in as the 43rd Governor on January 5, 1999. ===Polling=== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign=bottom !
